draft.title: Phases of the moon
card: The moon does not make its own light. It shines because its surface reflects sunlight.
The sun always lights half of the moon, the half facing it. The other half is dark.
The moon orbits the Earth about every 29.5 days. As it moves, we see a different amount of its lit half from Earth.
At new moon we see almost none of the lit half. At full moon we see all of it. The shape then shrinks back to new moon, and the cycle repeats.
draft.remember: The moon's phases come from how much of its lit half we can see as it orbits.

a.q: What causes the moon to change from a thin crescent to a full moon over about two weeks?
opts: We see more of the moon's lit half as it orbits
The Earth's shadow covers less of the moon
The moon makes more light as it moves
The sun lights more of the moon's surface
a.why: The sun always lights half of the moon. As the moon orbits, we see more of that lit half from Earth. Earth's shadow is not the cause of phases, and the moon makes no light of its own.
a.clue: Think about which half is lit and what we can see of it.

b.q: Priya watches the moon from her home in Darwin. On one night she sees a full moon. About how long until she sees the next full moon?
opts: About 29.5 days, after one full orbit of the Earth
About 7 days, after a quarter of an orbit
About 14 days, after half of an orbit
About 365 days, after the Earth orbits the sun
b.why: The cycle of phases repeats as the moon orbits the Earth, which takes about 29.5 days. After half an orbit, about 14 days, she would see a new moon instead. The year-long trip is the Earth's orbit of the sun, not the moon's cycle.
b.clue: The cycle of phases repeats once per orbit of the moon.

a.best: We see more of the moon's lit half as it orbits

b.best: About 29.5 days, after one full orbit of the Earth

problems.detail: The card says the moon orbits the Earth about every 29.5 days. One orbit relative to the stars takes about 27.3 days. The 29.5-day figure is the cycle of phases (new moon to new moon). It is safer to say 'the cycle of phases takes about 29.5 days' and not equate it with one orbit.
The right option pairs 29.5 days with 'one full orbit of the Earth'. That repeats the card's imprecision, since the moon's actual orbit takes about 27.3 days.
The clue, 'The cycle of phases repeats once per orbit of the moon', points straight to the only option that mentions one full orbit. A student can answer without knowing the length of the cycle.
The right option is the longest, and it is the only one with the exact figure from the card (29.5). It stands out from the rounder numbers in the other options.
